subject: Materials Science
title: Surface Area to Volume Ratio
description: A 60-second lesson on Surface Area to Volume Ratio.

hook.text: Cut a sugar cube into nanoparticles and its surface area could cover a football field — all from one tiny cube.

buildup.text: As particles shrink, the surface-to-volume ratio skyrockets — more surface means more reactivity.

discovery.text: Catalysts use nanoparticles because reactions happen on surfaces — more surface equals more chemistry per gram.

twist.text: Extreme surface area also means extreme reactivity — aluminum nanoparticles ignite spontaneously in air.

climax.text: This principle drives everything from better batteries to faster catalysts to more effective sunscreens.

punchline.text: Make it smaller, make more surface — surface is where the action happens.

quiz.question: Why are nanoparticles more chemically reactive than bulk materials?
options: Their enormous surface-to-volume ratio exposes more atoms for reactions
